source_tier: primary/regulatory (MARAD deepwater-port licence application + MARAD/USCG Draft EIS)
source_notes: Off-grid by design: the applicant's own MARAD licence application states 'The facility would have no connection to the electric power grid... Gas turbine generators with waste heat recovery units would be utilized to provide power and heat to the DWP.' The Draft EIS (April 2026) stationary-source list, explicitly 'inclusive of all phases', gives SIXTEEN Baker Hughes LT-16 (NovaLT16) gas-fired combustion turbines for POWER GENERATION project-wide (4/phase; per-phase description: four gas turbine generators on the Gas Treatment Platform, three operating + one standby, plus two essential generators on the Liquefaction Platform) = 270.4 MW installed nameplate at 16.9 MW/unit, ~202.8 MW at normal N+1 load. Far above the >50 MW threshold, and a REAL electricity-generating captive plant, not only shaft power. Separately (mechanical=True): EIGHT Siemens SGT-750 gas turbines as MR compressor drivers project-wide (2/phase) -- shaft power, NEVER summed into the generating MW. VENDOR CONFLICT, unresolved: the April-2026 Draft EIS and the June-2025 application both name Siemens SGT-750 as the compressor driver, whereas the March-2026 Baker Hughes press release was read as LM6000PF compressor trains; either a post-DEIS vendor change or a trade-press inaccuracy. It does not affect the captive verdict (mechanical drive is present either way). Final EIS text itself was not reachable (docket entries 403 without a session); the Draft is treated as authoritative for engineering facts since a FEIS is DEIS + comment responses, not a redesign.

source_tier: primary/regulatory (FERC Order Granting Authorization CP15-521) + trade (NS Energy)
source_notes: Captive power is DESIGN-STAGE and belongs to THIS unit-row (the FERC-authorized but never-built liquefaction project): gas turbines mechanically drive the propane-precool/mixed-refrigerant compressors, two per train x two trains = four turbines. FERC's July 2019 order condition #48 requires vendor datasheets for the 'MR/PR compressor gas turbine emission control system'; NS Energy independently: 'Fitted with two gas-fired turbine compressors, each train will have a nominal liquefaction capacity of 5Mtpa.' Mechanical drive (shaft power, no generator) -- in scope per Captive-power SOP 2, mechanical=True. YELLOW because no MW/HP rating for the turbines appears in any verified source (left undisclosed rather than invented) and the plant was never built (no FID). Scale precedent: this driver class on a 5+ MTPA C3MR train is conventionally well above 50 MW, but that is inference, not a cited figure.

source_tier: primary/regulatory (FERC Order Granting Authorization CP15-521) + trade (NS Energy)
source_notes: PROPAGATION ROW -- CaptiveGasPower is a project-level field, so the DB holds one value for TerminalID T100000130228 and it is written here too. The captive power itself does NOT belong to this operating import unit: the import terminal is grid-fed by Mississippi Power Co. (23,000 V line stepped to 4,160 V, per the 2019 DOE/FERC Final EIS Ch.2), vaporizes via ten submerged-combustion vaporizers (process heat, not power or drive), and its only on-site gas combustion is two 12 MW 'essential power backup' gas-turbine generators -- 24 MW total, below the >50 MW threshold and backup-only, so a clean negative on its own. The True value derives entirely from the proposed export project's mechanical-drive design (see the Export Terminal T1-T2 row). Read the two rows together.
